proposal: In unlocked own-node up_action only, publish completed out to the original parent CFV row immediately before the unchanged regret-update loop. All expressions/within-out order, strategy scheduling and other branches stay unchanged.

measured_motivation.limits: Measured rainbow diagnostic ranking, not a speed forecast or removable wall-time bound.

source_proof: GpuPlan::build assigns reachable action/chance scratch rows to disjoint even/odd level pools; unique current-level outputs cannot alias next-level child inputs. Cached fold/showdown terminal rows are allocated beyond both scratch pools.

Action edges advance the traversal level by one; every child of a queued reached action is reached and has a valid slot. Existing plan tests explicitly check unique same-level outputs, scratch/terminal separation and disjoint adjacent live levels.
All actual production CFVslot assignment sites found in the scoped gpuRust search are in GpuPlan::build. Continuation wrappers use that owned solver plan; no custom mutable CFV mapping is introduced.

Hence parent row store cannot change any later child value reload, including na>8uncached fallback. Same-level CUDA blocks also cannot overwrite each other's live inputs. Existing stream/graph dependencies make the earlier store invisible to later kernels until this launch completes.

Learning and CFV device allocations have separate owned CUDA buffers. No arithmetic, summation/reduction order, pointer qualifier, loop factor/arity, dtype, allocation, graph node, shared layout, quality or stopping change. Failed kernel updates have no rollback contract; valid ranges remain the scope.
potential_mechanism: Releasing parent addressing inputs earlier may change live ranges/register scheduling before regret stores. Actual resources and timing must establish any benefit.
